buffer_note: Every encoder in the CBR charts is asked for a 1 s buffer at the target rate; openh264 has no buffer setting. Measured at each stream's own achieved rate (the rate it is plotted at), on the 209 held-out clips of the 0.6.0 charts nanocodec exceeds one buffer on 25-38 % of points, the other references on 2-12 % and openh264 on 42 %. From 0.6.1 nanocodec re-codes any frame that would leave more than 1.15 buffers queued, and --strict-buffer holds it to exactly one buffer. The CBR charts will be re-measured on 0.6.1; the Fixed QP charts have no rate control and are not affected. Against 0.6.0's buffer, on the medium presets, the 1.15-buffer default costs +0.49 to +0.99 % over 150 frames and -0.04 to +2.24 % over 600 frames in BD-J (bits at equal quality), and strict mode +1.23 to +1.92 % over 150 frames and +1.59 to +2.72 % over 600 frames (one run per arm, no confidence interval; medium presets only).
